_V2_LABEL.NOINV: no inversion after fronted adverbial (EN order, 'Dessutom, vi måste')
_V2_LABEL.V3: adverb between subject and verb ('Vi också vill')
_V2_LABEL.EMB: main-clause negation order in subordinate clause ('att vi kan inte')

exclamation.label: exclamation mark ending a non-vocative sentence

rules.name: calques.lexicon
rules.rationale: INT: word-for-word renderings of English multi-word expressions and constructions where Swedish has a native alternative (named next to each entry). High precision, low recall: a hit is evidence, absence is not. Values are conservative log rate ratios from dev-train (<= 1.5 per hit), lowered for drift and O usage.
rules.source: literature A12, A16/§4.6, A18, C10; [exp] collocations.py candidates

groups._m4: calque 'på X basis' (EN 'on a X basis')
groups._m6: calque 'på samma gång' (EN 'at the same time')
groups._m7: calque 'det är tydligt att' (EN 'it is clear that')
groups._m12: calque 'när det rör' (EN 'as regards / when it concerns')
groups._m15: calque 'möjligt för X att' (EN 'possible for X to')
groups._m17: calque 'låt oss vara tydliga' (EN 'let us be clear')
groups._m28: calque 'vid en tid då' (EN 'at a time when')
groups._m30: calque 'i ett försök att' (EN 'in an attempt to')
groups._m31: calque 'bara rätt (och riktigt) att' (EN 'only right and proper')
groups._m35: calque sentence-initial 'Så vi/jag/det' (EN 'So we/I/it', no V2)
groups._m38: calque 'det är en fråga om' (EN 'it is a question of')

groups_raw._m4: calque 'på X basis' (EN 'on a X basis')
groups_raw._m6: calque 'på samma gång' (EN 'at the same time')
groups_raw._m7: calque 'det är tydligt att' (EN 'it is clear that')
groups_raw._m12: calque 'när det rör' (EN 'as regards / when it concerns')
groups_raw._m15: calque 'möjligt för X att' (EN 'possible for X to')
groups_raw._m17: calque 'låt oss vara tydliga' (EN 'let us be clear')
groups_raw._m28: calque 'vid en tid då' (EN 'at a time when')
groups_raw._m30: calque 'i ett försök att' (EN 'in an attempt to')
groups_raw._m31: calque 'bara rätt (och riktigt) att' (EN 'only right and proper')
groups_raw._m35: calque sentence-initial 'Så vi/jag/det' (EN 'So we/I/it', no V2)
groups_raw._m38: calque 'det är en fråga om' (EN 'it is a question of')

rules.name: calques.native_counterparts
rules.rationale: The native variant of a calque pair is itself O-leaning when the English source pushes translators to the calque (det är klart att vs det är tydligt att; inflytande över vs på).

groups._m0: native 'det är klart att' (vs 'det är tydligt att')

groups_raw._m0: native 'det är klart att' (vs 'det är tydligt att')

rules.name: calques.forsoka_att
rules.rationale: INT: EN 'try to V' -> 'försöka att V'; native Swedish takes a bare infinitive ('försöka göra'). The B variant has the same rate in both classes, so the choice model holds.

rules.name: calques.pied_piped_relative
rules.rationale: INT: EN 'in which / for which / from whom' -> 'i vilket / för vilka / från vilka'; native Swedish strands the preposition ('som ... i'), or uses 'där', 'vari', 'varav'. First written as a ChoiceRule against 'som', but 'som' carries no information (22 per 1000 in both classes) and its period-dependent rate only added noise (100-word AUC 0.48 on 2002-04), so only the calque is counted.
rules.label: pied-piped relative ''

rules.name: connpunct.native_connectives
rules.description: native connective adverbs (dessutom, därför, dock, därmed, inte minst ...)
rules.rationale: Explicitation predicts more connectives in T, but on EP dev originals use ~2.6x more native connective adverbs: Swedish argumentative speech places them in the middle field (V2), while translators only render connectives present in the English source (unique-items effect). Reversed w.r.t. Volansky's English result.
rules.source: literature D1/D2 [direction reversed on EP dev]; Tirkkonen-Condit (2004)

rules.name: connpunct.additive_ocksa
rules.rationale: Additive cohesion ('vi måste också ...') is a native Swedish argumentative habit in the middle field; English 'also/too/as well' is less frequent and often left unrendered. Same mechanism as native_connectives, kept separate because of its frequency (bursty) -> low weight.

rules.name: connpunct.calque_connectives
rules.description: Swedish equivalents of English discourse markers (i synnerhet, i själva verket ...)
rules.rationale: Interference: fixed English discourse markers (in particular, in fact, nevertheless, first of all, in summary, for this reason) are rendered by their dictionary equivalents, which native speakers use far less (they use framför allt, faktiskt, ändå, först, kort sagt instead).
rules.source: literature D1 (Volansky et al. 2015 cohesive markers), 4.3a

rules.name: connpunct.att_drop
rules.rationale: Explicitation: Swedish allows dropping 'att' after verbs of saying and thinking ('Jag tror det är viktigt'); translators retain it (English 'that' is also often absent, so this is normalisation to the written norm). Also spoken register.
rules.label: att dropped: ''

rules.name: connpunct.som_drop
rules.description: object relative without 'som' ('det arbete ni har gjort')
rules.rationale: The literature expects 'som'-retention (explicitation) in T; EP dev shows the reverse: English contact clauses ('the work you have done') are rendered with a zero relative ('det arbete ni har gjort'), i.e. interference beats explicitation.
rules.source: literature D1/3 ('som' retained) [direction reversed on EP dev; exp]

rules.name: connpunct.initial_och
rules.rationale: Interference: English speakers open sentences with 'And'; Swedish written and edited norm avoids sentence-initial 'Och', so the Swedish transcripts almost never have it while translators keep the source's sentence division.

rules.name: connpunct.initial_men
rules.rationale: Interference: English 'But' at sentence start is kept as 'Men'; Swedish speakers more often coordinate within the sentence (', men') or use 'dock' in the middle field. (Volansky found the opposite for English O vs T: the direction is source-language specific.)
rules.source: Volansky et al. (2015) positional tokens [direction differs]; [exp]

rules.name: connpunct.initial_adverbial_comma
rules.rationale: English sets off fronted adverbials with a comma; Swedish V2 does not ('Därför anser jag'). Only the punctuation is scored here: the V2 violation that often follows ('Dessutom, vi måste') belongs to the wordorder family.

rules.name: connpunct.clause_comma_omission
rules.rationale: English does not put a comma before restrictive 'because', 'while', 'which' and often not before 'but'; translators follow the source punctuation, while the Swedish norm of the period puts a comma before these clause linkers. The O rate rises over time (looser Swedish comma norms), hence weight 0.7.

rules.name: connpunct.written_out_abbrev
rules.description: 'till exempel/så kallad/till och med' written out vs 't.ex./s.k./t.o.m.'
rules.rationale: NORM / house style: translators follow the writing guidelines (Myndigheternas skrivregler) and write abbreviations out in running text; the Swedish transcripts (and MEPs' written explanations of vote) keep t.ex., dvs., bl.a. This is an orthographic convention of the two EP services rather than of translation as such: low weight, will not generalise beyond EP.

rules.name: connpunct.parenthetical_dash
rules.rationale: Source shining through: English speeches (as transcribed) make heavy use of dash-delimited asides; translators keep them, while Swedish transcribers break sentences or use commas. Partly a transcription convention of the English verbatim report, so low weight.
rules.source: Volansky et al. (2015) punctuation [exp for the dash]

rules.name: connpunct.explanatory_parens
rules.description: explanatory parentheses (no numbers, not document codes)
rules.rationale: Explicitation: parenthetical glosses and acronym expansions are typical of translations (Volansky: parentheses mark T).

rules.name: connpunct.exclamation
rules.rationale: Spoken rhetoric ('Vi lynchar inte Pinochet - vi dömer honom!', 'Tack för svaret!'): Swedish transcribers keep the exclamation; translations of English verbatim reports rarely have one outside the vocative. Partly a transcription convention (SPK), so low weight and small cap.

rules.name: starter.modal_particles
rules.rationale: Unique items: Swedish modal particles have no English trigger, so translators rarely create them (of course -> naturligtvis, not ju).

rules.name: starter.sent_len
rules.rationale: Translations from English keep long source sentences and add explicitation; the originals are edited speech. Weak (65% alone in the literature) and the sentence means vary by speaker more than independence assumes (text-mean sd at 500 words ~3 vs ~2 predicted), hence weight 0.5.

rules.name: particles.namligen
rules.rationale: UNQ: the explanatory modal particle 'nämligen' (Jag anser nämligen att ...) has no English counterpart (EN 'because/for' or nothing), so translators almost never create it; the appositive 'namely' use is excluded.

rules.name: particles.anda
rules.rationale: UNQ + SPK: 'ändå' is both a concessive adverb and a modal particle of shared expectation (Det är ändå viktigt); EN 'still/yet/nevertheless' are often rendered by 'dock/emellertid/trots detta', and the particle use has no trigger. O rate typed from 2000-04 (drift toward the test period).

rules.name: particles.alltsa
rules.rationale: UNQ + SPK: 'alltså' as a resumptive/inferential particle (Problemet är alltså ...) is a spoken-Swedish discourse marker; translators use it only for EN 'thus/so' and prefer 'således/därför'. O rate typed from 2000-04 because of drift; low cap.

rules.name: particles.stance
rules.description: stance adverbs 'egentligen/visserligen/i och för sig/i alla fall'
rules.rationale: UNQ: Swedish-specific stance/concession markers ('egentligen' = 'actually, when it comes down to it'; 'visserligen ... men'; 'i och för sig') with no stable English trigger; EN 'actually/admittedly/in any case' map to other items.

rules.name: particles.da_anaphoric
rules.rationale: UNQ + SPK: 'då' as an anaphoric connective/particle linking to the previous statement (Då måste vi ...; Vad finns det då för ...) is typical of Swedish argumentation; English mostly has no word or 'so/then'. The temporal/causal subjunction ('Då vi ...', ', då de ...') is excluded by requiring a finite verb right after sentence-initial 'Då' and no subject after post-verbal 'då'.

rules.name: particles.of_course
rules.rationale: Literature A7 predicts naturligtvis = T (EN 'of course' -> dictionary default 'naturligtvis'). On EP dev 'naturligtvis' is NOT more frequent in T, but the choice among the 'of course' adverbs is: native speakers spread over självklart/givetvis/förstås. Gives T presence evidence.

rules.name: particles.dvs
rules.rationale: Swedish speakers reformulate and specify on the fly with 'dvs.' (Swedish speech and edited speech); the English source rarely has 'that is/i.e.' at those points, so translators seldom add it. Pointed out by the error analysis of the starter engine. Possible overlap with a connectives family: small cap. O rate from 2000-04.
rules.source: [exp] (coordinator error analysis); literature D2 (O-leaning discourse markers)

rules.name: particles.particle_verbs
rules.description: Swedish-specific particle verbs (slå fast, ställa sig bakom, lyfta fram, ...)
rules.rationale: UNQ: idiomatic particle verbs whose image has no English counterpart (slå fast 'establish', ställa sig bakom 'endorse', lyfta fram 'highlight', gå ut på 'aim at') are produced by native speakers but not triggered by the English Latinate verb, which translators render with a single verb (fastställa, stödja, betona).
rules.source: literature 4.7, A16 note; Tirkkonen-Condit (2004) [exp for the item list]

rules.name: particles.ta_itu_med
rules.rationale: Translation-equivalent over-use: 'ta itu med' is the standard rendering of EN 'tackle/address/deal with', which are very frequent in EP English; native speakers spread over hantera, komma till rätta med, ta tag i, lösa.
rules.source: [exp]; literature 4.7 (particle verbs; direction reversed for this item)

rules.name: particles.generic_man
rules.rationale: UNQ: 'man' is the Swedish generic pronoun; English uses you/we/one/people/passive, which translators render as vi, ni, en, människor or a passive. O rate typed from 2000-04 because of drift; bursty per speaker, hence weight 0.5.

rules.name: particles.copular_det
rules.description: copular 'det är/var' and 'är/var det' (expletive, cleft, anaphoric det)
rules.rationale: Swedish fills the prefield and the subject slot with low-information 'det' (extraposition 'Det är viktigt att', clefts 'Det är vi som', anaphoric 'Det är bra'); English 'this is / we must / it is' renderings give 'detta är' or a personal subject in translation. High-frequency item: weight 0.5.

rules.name: particles.poss_1st
rules.rationale: INT: English possessive determiners are near-obligatory (our citizens, my country, our industry) where Swedish uses the definite form or a compound (medborgarna, hemlandet, läkemedelsindustrin); translators keep 'vår/min'.
rules.source: literature A11 (pronoun profile, [exp] direction); Volansky et al. (2015) pronouns

rules.name: particles.poss_3rd
rules.rationale: INT: EN his/her/its/their are rendered as hans/hennes/dess/deras where Swedish would use the definite form, a compound, or reflexive 'sin'. A cheaper 'sin vs deras' choice (same clause as a 3rd-person subject) showed no difference (professional translators get the reflexive right), so a rate is used.

rules.name: particles.han_hon
rules.rationale: INT/explicitation: English debate speakers refer back to the rapporteur, the Commissioner or a colleague with he/she, kept as han/hon in translation; Swedish speakers more often repeat the title (föredraganden, kommissionären) or use the name. Turn-structure dependent (replies to named members): low weight.
rules.source: literature A11 (pronoun profile, direction [exp]); hybrid-ML coefficients

rules.name: particles.ni_vs_man
rules.rationale: INT: EN generic 'you' (You can then go down to ...) is rendered 'ni' where a native speaker uses generic 'man'; EN address 'you' adds more 'ni'. Conditioning on the ni/man choice is less sensitive to how much a text addresses someone than a raw 'ni' rate, though EP address still inflates 'ni' in both classes.

rules.name: register.kommer_att_vs_ska
rules.rationale: Swedish marks intended/planned future and obligation with 'ska' and keeps 'kommer att' for prediction; English 'will' covers both, and translators render it with the dictionary equivalent 'kommer att' (NORM + INT). Both spellings of ska are counted, so the rule is robust to the house-style switch skall -> ska (which made the old starter.ska_vs_skall a spelling detector). Risk: att-drop ('kommer bli') grows in later originals; it is not counted as 'kommer att', which only weakens the rule.
rules.source: Danielsson (2003) skall/ska keyword [re-framed]; literature A2, A17, C7; [exp]

rules.name: register.skulle_vilja_vs_vill
rules.rationale: EN 'I would like to (thank/say/stress)' is rendered literally as 'jag skulle vilja'; the native performative is 'jag vill tacka'. Polite O speakers also use it, so the evidence is a shift in share, not a calque detector. Overlaps calque c42: keep it in one family only.

rules.name: register.tycker_vs_anser
rules.rationale: 'tycka' (personal evaluative opinion) is a Swedish-specific distinction with no English counterpart; EN 'think/believe/consider/feel' is rendered with the formal 'anse'. Danielsson's O cluster 'tycker att det här'.

rules.name: register.valdigt_vs_mycket
rules.rationale: EN 'very' -> the formal 'mycket'; the spoken-register 'väldigt' is a native choice translators avoid (NORM + SPK). Diachronic: väldigt is falling in edited EP originals, so the cap is small.
rules.source: Danielsson (2003) O keyword väldigt; literature A4, A21

rules.name: register.sjalvklart
rules.rationale: Swedish political speech marks shared ground with 'självklart' (adjective-derived, more colloquial); EN 'of course / naturally' is rendered with the dictionary equivalents 'naturligtvis/givetvis', so translations rarely contain 'självklart' (NORM + unique-item effect).
rules.source: literature A7 / G10 [refined on EP dev]; [exp]

rules.name: register.dem_har_rate
rules.rationale: Literature (A1) predicts den här = O. EP originals are edited to written norm (denna/detta), while translators of oral English 'this' often keep the spoken 'den/det här'. Direction reversed on EP; expect it to be weaker or flip outside EP.
rules.source: Danielsson (2003) [direction reversed on EP dev]; docs/ENGINE.md findings

rules.name: register.bland_annat
rules.rationale: Unique item: 'bland annat' is Swedish's routine marker of a non-exhaustive list; English marks it differently ('including', 'such as', rare 'inter alia'), which translators render 'inklusive/däribland/t.ex.' (inklusive/däribland O 0.11 vs T 0.30 /1000w).

rules.name: register.samt
rules.rationale: Unique item: formal Swedish 'samt' ('and also', list-final) has no distinct English trigger; EN 'and' -> 'och'. Literature A25 guessed T (bureaucratese); on EP dev it is an O marker.
rules.source: Tirkkonen-Condit (2004) unique items; literature A25 [direction reversed]

rules.name: register.bra
rules.rationale: Spoken/neutral evaluative 'bra' ('det är bra att', 'ett bra betänkande') is the native default; translators render EN 'good/welcome/positive' with more formal or more specific adjectives.

rules.name: stats.long_words
rules.description: share of long words (> 6 letters, the LIX criterion)
rules.rationale: The long-word component of LIX, without its sentence-length term (starter.sent_len already models that). Simplification predicts shorter words in T; on EP dev the OPPOSITE holds: translations from English have more 7-13-letter words (nominal style: derived abstract nouns and definite forms such as 'genomförandet', 'tillämpningen', EU terminology), while the very longest words (16+ letters, closed compounds) are slightly more frequent in originals. T > O in every year 1997-2004, but the level rises for both classes from 2000 (drift risk on test).
rules.source: Björnsson (1968) LIX; Volansky et al. (2015) mean word length 66% [direction from dev]; literature C6/E5

rules.name: stats.av_nominal
rules.rationale: Transfer of English 'the implementation/use/introduction of X' as a definite nominalisation + av-phrase; native Swedish prefers a verb clause ('att genomföra'), a compound or an s-genitive. Disjoint from stats.av_other (every 'av' is counted once).
rules.source: Nilsson (2004); Danielsson (2003) (av among T keywords); literature A6/C5

rules.name: stats.av_other
rules.rationale: English of-phrases ('a part of', 'the rights of', 'aspects of our culture') and by-agents of be-passives are rendered with 'av' where Swedish prefers compounds, s-genitives or s-passives without agent: the preposition is over-represented in translations. A lexical rate, but kept here as the periphrasis/compounding indicator of the simplification family.

rules.name: wordorder.fronted_theme
rules.description: topicalised non-subject in the prefield (V2 inversion): which kind
rules.rationale: Hasselgård (2004): V2 languages put non-subjects in the prefield far more often than English, and translators keep the English Theme. Each sentence whose opening the closed-list heuristic classifies as a fronted non-subject + finite verb contributes ln(p_T/p_O) of its type (one half of a multinomial 'which opening was chosen' model over classifiable openings; see OPENING_P). O: topicalised deictic/causal adverbs (därför, nu, då, samtidigt, här, däremot: -0.96), fronted object det/detta (-1.6, B3), fronted NPs, PPs (weak). T: inversion after structuring conjuncts that mirror a sentence-initial English adverbial ('Firstly,' 'Finally,' 'However,'), and fronted adverbial clauses ('If ..., we ...'): fronting is not O per se, only Swedish-initiated topicalisation is. Resumptive 'så' (B4) is not O on trn (merged into fronted clauses).
rules.source: literature B1, B3, B4; Hasselgård (2004); Bohnacker & Rosén (2008); [exp] for the INV_CONJ / INV_SUB split

rules.name: wordorder.subject_theme
rules.description: subject in the prefield: pronoun / NP / det / demonstrative / cleft
rules.rationale: Other half of the opening model: subject-first declaratives (B1, T: English Theme kept; pronoun and NP subjects lumped because each drifts with year and speaker mix, the sum is stable and only weakly T), 'Detta är' (EN 'This is'), pseudo-clefts 'Vad vi behöver är' (EN 'What we need is') -> T; expletive 'Det är/finns' and clefts 'Det är X som' (B2, B8: Swedish fills the prefield with light 'det' and focuses with clefts) -> O.
rules.source: literature B1, B2, B8; Hasselgård (2004); [exp] for S_DEM / PSEUDO_CLEFT

rules.name: wordorder.v2_violation
rules.description: English word order leaking into Swedish (V3 / no inversion / embedded negation)
rules.rationale: Interference with English SVO: a fronted adverbial followed by subject + verb ('Med andra ord, de är ...', 'Slutligen, kommissionen är ...'), a sentence adverb between subject and finite verb ('Jag verkligen hoppas'), and main-clause negation order after a subjunction ('att jag har inte', native 'att jag inte har'). Rare in professional translation but precise. trn dev.500.bal: no-inversion openings O 4 / T 33 (0.006 / 0.047 per 1000 words); embedded negation order dev.500.all O 0 / T 39 (0 / 0.011); V3 O 0 / T 2. Per hit 1.5 (judgement; observed ln ratio ~2.4, O counts too small to trust).
